panama_CNR_1:
"Goal/Purpose": "Expand the Panama Canal PIEA to promote sustainable land-use management inside the Panama Canal watershed, support implementation of relevant objectives and targets of the Indicative Environmental Land-Use Plan for the Panama Canal Watershed (PIOTA–CHCP), and contribute to decarbonization, climate resilience, and sustainable land-use in the basin.",
"Action/Intervention": "Expand the Panama Canal PIEA through the PBP Agreement, leveraging the PIEA incentive model to ensure performance-based implementation; provide PIEA incentive packages targeting small scale producers and local communities, including equitably women and men among them; foster conservation and restoration of prioritized forest ecosystems; implement sustainable agriculture packages, including agro-forestry and silvopastoral systems; support family agriculture and alternative livelihoods; and expand the Conservation PES Programme in the Panama Canal watershed.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Panama Canal watershed / basin, including prioritized forest ecosystems and the territorial and environmental management area covered by PIOTA–CHCP.",
"Target Audience": "Small scale producers and local communities, including equitably women and men among them; ACP as the implementing institution of the existing PIEA Programme.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Performance-based implementation of the expanded PIEA Programme; conservation and restoration of prioritized forest ecosystems; implementation of sustainable agriculture packages; support for family agriculture and alternative livelihoods; expansion of the Conservation PES Programme in the Panama Canal watershed; and support for relevant PIOTA–CHCP objectives and targets related to decarbonization, climate resilience, and sustainable land-use."
panama_CNR_2:

"Action/Intervention": "Develop the institutional and management structure to enable implementation of the PIEA incentives package model outside the Panama Canal watershed; implement activities to develop such institutional and management structure as part of Output 2, in alignment with Panama’s REDD+ NS implementation approach and Executive Decree No. 479 of April 23, 2013; use relevant PIOTAs to guide implementation of the PIEA package of incentives; finance the actual implementation of the PIEA package of incentives outside the Panama Canal watershed under a socially inclusive and gender-responsive approach.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Outside the Panama Canal watershed; water basins as the primary units for environmental and territorial planning.",
"Target Audience": "Not explicitly specified.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Implementation of the PIEA package of incentives outside the Panama Canal watershed, guided by relevant PIOTAs and supported by an institutional and management structure, under a socially inclusive and gender-responsive approach."
panama_CNR_3:
"Goal/Purpose": "Develop the institutional and management structure to implement a socially inclusive and gender-responsive incentives program targeting Indigenous Peoples, Afro Descendant communities, and small-scale producers, tailored to their socio-economic characteristics, relationship with forest ecosystems, and traditional knowledge, and linked to measurable outcomes.",
"Action/Intervention": "Design and implement an incentives Programme; develop institutional and management structures; implement instruments to stimulate the conservation and sustainable management of forests and the management and sustainable use of non-timber forest products; incorporate livelihood activities compatible with protected area management, including community nurseries for native seedlings, value chains for NTFP such as honey, seeds, fibers, and handicrafts, and low-impact ecotourism activities such as guiding, trails, and signage; align all activities with protected area zoning and management plans; follow PBP logic linking payments to measurable outcomes.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Forest ecosystems and protected areas (PA), including non-timber forest product management and use.",
"Target Audience": "Indigenous Peoples, Afro Descendant communities, and small-scale producers, including women and men among them.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Stimulated conservation and sustainable management of forests; sustainable management and use of non-timber forest products; promotion of conservation efforts through livelihoods compatible with protected area management; environmental integrity and sustainability; payments linked to measurable outcomes."

"Action/Intervention": "Financing the National Restoration Programme; efforts to enrich secondary forests; promoting native regeneration and reforestation with native species; fostering ecosystem connectivity through biological corridors; increasing nursery production; in protected areas and their buffer zones, enhancing carbon stocks through ecological restoration, strengthening effective management, improving landscape connectivity by establishing biological corridors, and promoting Other Effective Area-Based Conservation Measures (OECMs) in buffer zones; aligning all interventions with protected area zoning and management plans.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Forests, including secondary forests, protected areas, and their buffer zones.",
"Target Audience": "Not explicitly specified in the target.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Enhanced forest carbon stocks, improved ecosystem and landscape connectivity through biological corridors, strengthened effective management in protected areas, and promotion of OECMs in buffer zones."
panama_CNR_5:

"Action/Intervention": "Design an integrated forest fire management Programme; develop and execute annual fire prevention and control plans; establish and maintain firebreaks; restore fire-affected or fire-prone areas such as canal grass-invaded land and tackle other ignition drivers; conduct continuous monitoring for early detection and rapid response; coordinate actions by MiAMBIENTE in partnership with ACP, firefighters and other relevant institutions, with the active participation of local communities.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Forest ecosystems, including the Panama Canal Basin watershed and fire-affected or fire-prone areas such as canal grass-invaded land.",
"Target Audience": "MiAMBIENTE, ACP, firefighters, other relevant institutions, and local communities, such as Indigenous Peoples, Afro Descendants and local communities, including equitably women and men among them.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Reduced GHG emissions from forest fires, protected forest carbon stocks, enhanced resilience of forest ecosystems and dependent communities, and effective inter-institutional collaboration with active participation of local communities."

panama_HR_1:
"Goal/Purpose": "Define, prioritize, implement, track, adjust, and consolidate mitigation policies and measures by sector to reduce GHG emissions, strengthen national mitigation governance and coordination, and ensure continuity of mitigation actions beyond 2035.",
"Action/Intervention": "Define a prioritized portfolio of policies and measures by sector with institutional leads, time horizon, and indicative contribution to GHG reduction using up-to-date GHG projections; strengthen the use of the ReNAM within the National Climate Transparency Platform for registration and tracking of mitigation actions through technical guidelines, accompaniment, and inter-institutional coordination agreements; analyze the technical, institutional, and economic feasibility of the main mitigation measures identified; establish formal mechanisms of inter-institutional coordination for mitigation implementation; implement pilot mitigation projects and programs in prioritized sectors (energy, waste, agriculture, and industrial processes); formalize implementation agreements with sectoral entities and key actors defining execution commitments, technical roles, and tracking mechanisms; technically accompany sectoral entities for the launch of prioritized mitigation measures; activate existing or under-development economic and financial instruments to support execution of viable mitigation measures; adjust the mitigation-measures portfolio based on observed results; adjust economic incentives, institutional arrangements, and technical guidelines that facilitate sustained adoption of scalable mitigation measures; strengthen coherence between mitigation, sectoral planning, and territorial planning so new public and private investments consider GHG-reduction criteria; review the national emissions-reduction trajectory against the required trajectory to identify gaps and guide corrective decisions; reinforce inter-institutional coordination to close gaps by concentrating efforts on actions with the greatest contribution potential; consolidate implemented mitigation measures within permanent instruments of sectoral and climate planning.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Climate mitigation; sectoral and territorial planning; National Climate Transparency Platform and ReNAM; prioritized sectors: energy, waste, agriculture, and industrial processes.",
"Target Audience": "Sectoral entities, institutional leads, inter-institutional coordination bodies, key actors involved in implementation agreements, and public and private investment actors.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "A prioritized and feasible portfolio of mitigation measures with defined institutional leads, timelines, and indicative GHG-reduction contributions; strengthened national registration and tracking of mitigation actions through ReNAM; formalized coordination, roles, responsibilities, and information flows among sectoral entities; pilot projects and prioritized mitigation measures launched in key sectors; economic and financial instruments activated to support implementation; mitigation measures adjusted based on observed results and emissions-gap analysis; stronger alignment of mitigation with sectoral and territorial planning and investment decisions; and mitigation measures consolidated in permanent planning instruments to ensure continuity beyond 2035."
panama_HR_2:
"Goal/Purpose": "Update and execute the National Forest Restoration Program at scale by validating a national baseline, defining quantitative pathways and priority territories, establishing effective-conservation arrangements for restored areas, reorienting agricultural programs toward silvopastoral and agroforestry systems, eliminating unplanned agricultural expansion that implies forest conversion within corridors, implementing restoration traceability and monitoring systems, restoring mangroves, strengthening conservation effectiveness, and ensuring verifiable LULUCF accounting.",
"Action/Intervention": "Validate a national baseline quantifying and characterizing restorable degraded areas, areas to be placed under effective conservation, and farms/agricultural landscapes eligible for productive restoration; disaggregate the target into pathways of 100,000 ha total, 2,500 ha mangrove, and 25,000 ha agricultural, including gaps, priority territories, and preliminary annual targets by type; delimit and validate the Azuero, Coclé, and Veraguas corridors, approve functional zoning, and define land-use rules and intervention priorities; define effective-conservation guidelines for restored areas, including conservation agreements with landowners, community co-management where applicable, surveillance and compliance mechanisms, and management leads, and integrate these into SINAP/OECM as appropriate or equivalent conservation arrangements in productive landscapes; reorient agricultural programs and incentives to implement silvopastoral and agroforestry systems on prioritized farms, with productive-performance targets of at least 20% productivity increase and eligibility criteria linked to corridor zoning and non-conversion of forests; define and launch an operational mechanism to eliminate unplanned agricultural expansion implying forest conversion within corridors through municipal land-use planning and zoning guidelines, satellite-based land-use-change traceability, and inter-institutionally coordinated control and compliance measures; design, implement, and monitor a traceability system for restoration actions aligned with existing national systems and national/international reporting requirements; approve and implement an intervention plan for restoration of 2,500 ha of mangrove, including site selection, permits, agreements with communities/users, technical execution, and post-restoration protection and monitoring; execute the program with explicit annual targets, prioritizing interventions by corridor and ensuring each intervention has an associated effective-conservation instrument; implement silvopastoral/agroforestry systems through agricultural extension with technical assistance, access to inputs, and productive follow-up; operationalize the zero-unplanned-expansion mechanism through periodic land-cover-change monitoring, territorial early warnings, coordinated corrective measures, and semi-annual corridor reports with public/administrative traceability; strengthen and evaluate conservation arrangements and adjust incentives and management rules according to corridor performance; adjust the restoration portfolio to prioritize interventions with greater carbon performance and permanence; carry out verification across hectares restored by type, effective conservation, productivity increase on intervened farms, compliance with zero unplanned expansion in corridors, and LULUCF accounting.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "National forest restoration areas; restorable degraded areas; areas to be placed under effective conservation; farms and agricultural landscapes eligible for productive restoration; mangroves; the Azuero, Coclé, and Veraguas corridors; productive landscapes within corridors.",
"Target Audience": "National Forest Restoration Program implementers; landowners; communities/users; management leads; agricultural programs and extension services; prioritized farms; municipalities; inter-institutional authorities responsible for land-use planning, monitoring, control, compliance, conservation arrangements, and national reporting systems.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Validated national baseline and quantified pathways for 100,000 ha total restoration, including 2,500 ha of mangrove and 25,000 ha of agricultural restoration; validated corridors with approved zoning, land-use rules, and intervention priorities; restored areas covered by effective-conservation instruments; implementation of silvopastoral and agroforestry systems on prioritized farms with at least 20% productivity increase; elimination of unplanned agricultural expansion implying forest conversion within corridors through operational monitoring and compliance; functioning restoration traceability system aligned with reporting requirements; approved and implemented mangrove restoration plan with post-restoration protection and monitoring; measurable annual progress by corridor; strengthened conservation arrangements reducing reversal risks; restoration portfolio adjusted for greater carbon performance and permanence; verification of hectares restored, effective conservation, farm productivity increase, compliance with zero unplanned expansion, and LULUCF accounting of at least 1 million tCO2e."
panama_HR_3:
"Goal/Purpose": "Ensure minimum standards of effective conservation through the review and update of the regulatory, normative, and operational framework of SINAP; expand SINAP to 40% terrestrial and 60% marine; strengthen effective conservation inside and outside formal protected areas through OECM and complementary arrangements; align the National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan as an enabling instrument of the Nature Pledge; develop integrated management in 10 strategic watersheds; guarantee coherence among conservation, land-use planning, local development, and cultural safeguards; and permanently incorporate effective management of SINAP and OECM into national, budgetary, and sectoral planning instruments beyond 2035.",
"Action/Intervention": "Review and update the regulatory, normative, and operational framework of SINAP; carry out a national diagnosis of effective management of terrestrial, marine, and continental protected areas, identifying gaps in planning, financing, personnel, control, monitoring, and community participation; define a technical roadmap for SINAP expansion to 40% terrestrial and 60% marine, prioritizing areas of high ecological value, connectivity, and climate resilience and incorporating criteria of effective-management feasibility and sustainable financing before new declarations; identify, evaluate, and recognize OECM and complementary arrangements in indigenous, private, and community territories and integrate them into the national conservation system; update and align the National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan with the Nature Pledge's governance, financing, incentives, and information-management frameworks; select and prioritize 10 strategic watersheds for integrated management plans; strengthen SINAP's operational capacities through investment in personnel, equipment, control and surveillance, and co-management mechanisms; develop, approve, and implement integrated management plans in the 10 priority watersheds with clear zoning, control mechanisms, community participation, and alignment with municipal and sectoral plans; channel permanent financing for SINAP management through the Fondo Panamá Natural and other mechanisms; periodically evaluate the effectiveness of management of protected areas and OECM using ecological, social, and governance indicators and adjust management plans, institutional arrangements, and resource allocation according to results; guarantee articulation among SINAP, indigenous territories, and local governments; verify compliance with coverage goals and effective management of SINAP and OECM, including ecological performance, governance, and financial sustainability; incorporate effective management of SINAP and OECM on a permanent basis into national, budgetary, and sectoral planning instruments.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "SINAP (National System of Protected Areas); terrestrial, marine, and continental protected areas; Other Effective area-based Conservation Measures (OECM); indigenous, private, and community territories; 10 strategic watersheds; areas of high ecological value; areas prioritized for connectivity and climate resilience.",
"Target Audience": "SINAP; protected areas and OECM managers; indigenous territories; private and community territories; local governments; municipal and sectoral planning authorities; Fondo Panamá Natural; institutions responsible for the National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan and the Nature Pledge.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Minimum standards of effective conservation ensured; national diagnosis of management gaps completed; technical roadmap for expansion to 40% terrestrial and 60% marine defined; OECM and complementary arrangements identified, evaluated, recognized, and integrated into the national conservation system; National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan updated and aligned with the Nature Pledge; 10 strategic watersheds selected and prioritized and integrated management plans developed, approved, and implemented; strengthened operational capacities of SINAP; permanent financing channeled for SINAP management; periodic evaluation of protected areas and OECM management effectiveness conducted with adjustments based on results; coherence ensured among conservation, land-use planning, local development, and cultural safeguards; compliance with coverage and effective-management goals verified; and effective management of SINAP and OECM permanently incorporated into national, budgetary, and sectoral planning instruments beyond 2035."
panama_HR_4:
"Goal/Purpose": "Conserve priority native species and manage human-wildlife conflicts through updated prioritization, identification of critical conflict areas, implementation of management measures, institutional strengthening, monitoring, territorial scaling, protocol formalization, operational integration, and permanent updating mechanisms.",
"Action/Intervention": "Update and validate a national list of priority native species for conservation using criteria of extinction risk, ecological value, territorial distribution, and level of human-wildlife conflict; identify and delimit five critical areas of human-wildlife conflict and analyze causes, actors involved, socio-economic impacts, and institutional capacities; implement conflict management measures in prioritized critical areas, including prevention protocols, compensation, risk management, and strengthening local capacities for coexistence; review the institutional base and verify the need to establish a monitoring system for priority species and human-wildlife conflicts with indicators of population status, genetic diversity, and reduction of incidents, interoperable with national environmental information systems; scale up species-management and human-wildlife coexistence approaches to new priority territories, strengthening articulation with SINAP management plans, biological corridors, and productive landscapes; formalize national protocols through administrative and technical instruments of MiAMBIENTE, defining institutional responsibilities, activation criteria, inter-institutional coordination mechanisms, and territorial application guidelines; integrate conservation and conflict management programs into the regular operational plans of SINAP and the biodiversity and wildlife directorates with annual planning, recurrent budget allocation, and continuous technical follow-up; establish a permanent mechanism for updating priority species and critical conflict areas based on scientific evidence and continuous monitoring.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Native species conservation, human-wildlife conflict management, priority territories, SINAP management plans, biological corridors, productive landscapes, and national environmental information systems.",
"Target Audience": "MiAMBIENTE, SINAP, the biodiversity and wildlife directorates, institutions involved in inter-institutional coordination, local capacities in prioritized critical areas, and actors involved in human-wildlife conflict management.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "A validated national list of priority native species; identification and delimitation of five critical human-wildlife conflict areas; implementation of prevention, compensation, risk management, and coexistence measures in prioritized areas; verification of the need for a monitoring system with indicators on population status, genetic diversity, and incident reduction; scaled-up species-management and coexistence approaches in new priority territories; formalized national management protocols; integration of programs into regular operational plans with annual planning, recurrent budget allocation, and continuous technical follow-up; and a permanent mechanism for periodic updating of priority species and critical conflict areas."
panama_HR_5:
"Goal/Purpose": "Control illegal wildlife trafficking in prioritized regions of the country through coordinated inter-institutional action, while integrating health-risk and conservation criteria, strengthening legal and sustainable trade controls, improving information systems, and ensuring stable operational capacity.",
"Action/Intervention": "Identify and prioritize at least five regions with high incidence of illegal wildlife trafficking; establish inter-institutional operational coordination protocols among MiAMBIENTE, MINSA, Customs, and security agencies; train park rangers, health personnel, and security forces in species identification, safe handling of seized wildlife, and zoonotic risk prevention; implement coordinated and permanent control operations in prioritized regions; strengthen control mechanisms for legal and sustainable species trade through traceability, permit compliance, and respect for traditional uses of indigenous peoples and local communities; integrate operational and control information into national environmental and risk-information systems; evaluate effectiveness of control mechanisms and coordination to identify gaps; adjust protocols, administrative procedures, and regulatory frameworks based on lessons learned and newly identified threats; define and ensure stable allocation of human, logistical, and operational resources through institutional budgets and operational plans; consolidate a national interoperable system for registration, analysis, and follow-up of illegal wildlife trafficking cases and zoonotic-risk events.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Wildlife trafficking control, biodiversity conservation, zoonotic risk management, legal and sustainable species trade, and environmental, health, and security information systems in prioritized regions of the country.",
"Target Audience": "MiAMBIENTE, MINSA, Customs, security agencies, park rangers, health personnel, security forces, indigenous peoples and local communities, and institutions managing environmental, health, and security information systems.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "At least five high-incidence regions prioritized; inter-institutional coordination protocols established; field and control personnel trained; permanent coordinated control operations implemented; stronger traceability and permit compliance in legal and sustainable species trade; operational data integrated into national systems; effectiveness of measures evaluated and gaps identified; protocols, procedures, and regulatory frameworks adjusted; stable human, logistical, and operational resources allocated; and a national interoperable system established to monitor trends, routes, zoonotic-risk events, and effectiveness of control measures."
panama_HR_6:
"Goal/Purpose": "Identify and prioritize the main pathways for the introduction of invasive alien species at the national level; define inter-institutional coordination on invasive alien species; strengthen biosecurity and prevention controls at critical entry points; implement early-detection and rapid-warning systems for priority invasive alien species; develop and execute early-response plans; and integrate generated information into national environmental and risk-information systems to allow evaluation of reductions in the rate of introduction and establishment.",
"Action/Intervention": "Use existing information from MiAMBIENTE, MIDA, Customs, and ARAP to identify and prioritize introduction pathways; define a basic scheme for inter-institutional coordination articulated with existing mechanisms for plant health, animal health, and environmental control, without creating new bodies during this phase; strengthen biosecurity and prevention controls at ports, airports, and prioritized borders using environmental- and health-risk criteria for invasive alien species; implement early-detection and rapid-warning systems in protected areas, productive zones, and aquatic ecosystems using existing monitoring and surveillance capacities; develop and execute early-response plans including containment, control, or eradication measures depending on species type and territorial context; integrate information from controls and responses into national environmental and risk-information systems.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "National level; critical entry points into the country (ports, airports, and prioritized borders); protected areas; productive zones; aquatic ecosystems; plant health, animal health, and environmental control.",
"Target Audience": "MiAMBIENTE, MIDA, Customs, ARAP, and institutions involved in plant health, animal health, environmental control, monitoring, surveillance, and risk-information systems.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Main introduction pathways for invasive alien species are identified and prioritized; a basic inter-institutional coordination scheme is defined; biosecurity and prevention controls at critical entry points are strengthened; early-detection and rapid-warning systems for priority invasive alien species are implemented; early-response plans are developed and executed; information is integrated into national environmental and risk-information systems; and reductions in the rate of introduction and establishment can be evaluated."
panama_HR_7:
"Goal/Purpose": "By 2035, Panama will reduce pollution and its cumulative effects by reducing by at least 50% the excess nutrients released into the environment and the risks associated with the use of pesticides, fungicides, and hazardous chemicals, complemented by a significant increase in the adoption of clean technologies in productive sectors.",
"Action/Intervention": "Prioritize a limited set of watersheds and critical territories where pollution by nutrients and chemicals represents greater environmental, health, or economic risks; identify the national technological gap for the reduction of pollution by chemicals and nutrients and map clean technologies available internationally that are not yet present or widespread in Panama; define a national pathway for the progressive reduction of risks from chemicals and nutrients, with clear milestones at 2030 and 2035, identifying priority sectors, types of instruments to be used, and expected levels of intervention, without yet initiating implementation at the national scale; align the chemicals- and nutrients-reduction pathway with the analysis of perverse and positive incentives in Target 14; design very focused pilot interventions in one or two prioritized territories to test combinations of technical assistance, incentive adjustments, and institutional arrangements; implement integrated territorial interventions in prioritized watersheds and productive zones, combining the progressive reduction of the use of polluting inputs, integrated nutrient management, and the adoption of practices and technologies of lower environmental impact; technically accompany producers, agro-industries, and industrial actors in the transition toward less polluting productive practices; apply in the intervened territories the economic incentives and technical support prioritized under Target 14; scale up the adoption of clean technologies and low-impact nutrient-management practices to new territories and productive sectors; focus additional actions on territories or sectors that still present elevated levels of pollution by chemicals and nutrients, reinforcing combinations of clean technologies, incentives, and environmental control.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Watersheds, critical territories, marine-coastal, restoration territories, productive zones, productive sectors, critical sectors, new territories, and sectors with elevated levels of pollution by chemicals and nutrients.",
"Target Audience": "Panama; producers; agro-industries; industrial actors.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "At least 50% reduction in excess nutrients released into the environment by 2035; reduction in the risks associated with the use of pesticides, fungicides, and hazardous chemicals; significant increase in the adoption of clean technologies in productive sectors; progressive reduction of the use of polluting inputs; adoption of low-impact nutrient-management practices; reduction of pollutant loads in prioritized territories."
