panama_HR_9:
"Goal/Purpose": "Update, harmonize, strengthen, and approve Panama’s legal, administrative, policy, and institutional frameworks for access to genetic resources, DSI, FPIC, and benefit-sharing, while ensuring continuous participation of indigenous peoples and local communities, coherence with international standards, and compliance with the Nagoya Protocol and the Cali Fund.",
"Action/Intervention": "Carry out a comparative legal analysis on frameworks for access to genetic resources, DSI, and benefit-sharing; identify existing legal, administrative, and policy frameworks in Panama requiring updating or harmonization; evaluate the functioning of the existing access system through review of contracts, agreed and delivered benefits, processing times, and compliance with FPIC; design participatory national guidelines for FPIC considering gender equity and in coordination with indigenous peoples and local communities; strengthen technical and institutional capacities in competent entities for management, compliance monitoring, and benefit negotiation; approve a legal and administrative framework that establishes mandatory review procedures for new laws and policies, creates the National Registry of Applications and Contracts, defines the benefit-sharing mechanism, adopts official contract templates, and establishes periodic compliance audits with mandatory application from 2028 onward; institutionalize permanent dialogue processes with indigenous peoples and local communities; establish clear procedures for benefit management including agreements, funds, or redistribution mechanisms; implement national monitoring and reporting mechanisms.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Access to genetic resources, Digital Sequence Information (DSI), free, prior and informed consent (FPIC), benefit-sharing, and governance/legal-administrative frameworks in Panama.",
"Target Audience": "Competent entities in Panama; indigenous peoples and local communities; entities involved in the governance and management of access to genetic resources and benefits.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Updated and harmonized frameworks incorporating DSI, FPIC, and benefit-sharing mechanisms; approved legal and administrative framework with mandatory application from 2028 onward; creation of the National Registry of Applications and Contracts; adoption of official contract templates; establishment of periodic compliance audits; institutionalized permanent dialogue with indigenous peoples and local communities; clear procedures for benefit management; strengthened technical and institutional capacities; national monitoring and reporting mechanisms in place; at least 80% of the relevant new frameworks fully comply with the Nagoya Protocol and the Cali Fund."
panama_HR_10:
"Goal/Purpose": "Identify and prioritize productive sectors and consumption patterns with the greatest environmental, material, and climate footprint, and progressively establish, implement, strengthen, expand, and integrate corporate commitments on sustainable production and consumption, with coherence to enabling economic, financial, regulatory, monitoring, reporting, and public-private dialogue mechanisms.",
"Action/Intervention": "Identify and prioritize sectors and consumption patterns with the greatest footprint; design a framework of gradual corporate commitments on sustainable production and consumption with progressive levels of ambition differentiated by sector and priority areas such as circular economy, waste reduction, and efficiency in resource use; define minimum credibility and traceability criteria for corporate commitments, including guidelines on acceptable types of action and minimum required evidence; establish an articulation pathway between corporate commitments and economic, financial, and regulatory instruments; install a mechanism of structured dialogue with high-impact companies and strategic sectoral actors; progressively implement prioritized corporate commitments and accompany high-impact companies in adopting sustainable production and consumption practices; strengthen technical and management capacities in high-impact companies; selectively apply enabled economic and financial instruments to incentivize compliance; strengthen performance requirements associated with corporate commitments; expand adoption of corporate commitments to more high-impact companies and sectors; close persistent gaps in lagging sectors or companies through regulation, differentiated incentives, and corrective measures; integrate adopted commitments and practices into mechanisms for monitoring, reporting, and public-private dialogue.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Productive sectors and consumption patterns with the greatest environmental, material, and climate footprint; priority areas including circular economy, waste reduction, efficiency in resource use, pollution, resource use, waste generation, and risks to health and ecosystems.",
"Target Audience": "High-impact companies; strategic sectoral actors; prioritized sectors and companies; lagging sectors or companies; corporate actors adopting sustainable production and consumption commitments.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "A validated and progressively implemented framework of corporate commitments on sustainable production and consumption; strengthened technical and management capacities in high-impact companies; incentivized compliance through economic and financial instruments; progressively stronger performance requirements based on implementation evidence and sector maturity; expanded adoption of commitments across more high-impact companies and sectors; persistent gaps addressed in lagging sectors or companies; and stable integration of commitments and practices into monitoring, reporting, and public-private dialogue mechanisms."
panama_HR_11:
"Goal/Purpose": "Design, validate, and expand a standardized national methodology for the characterization of urban solid waste and food waste; consolidate and institutionalize an official national baseline on their generation and composition; and use this information to prioritize territorial and sectoral interventions for waste and food-waste reduction.",
"Action/Intervention": "Design and validate a standardized national methodology aligned with international standards and adaptable to diverse municipal contexts; select representative municipalities and execute pilot studies for the characterization of waste and food waste; ensure methodological consistency and collect data disaggregated by type of waste, source, and territory; train municipal technical teams, waste operators, and key actors in applying the methodology; expand the methodology nationally, prioritizing municipalities with greater waste generation and critical food-waste flows; consolidate collected data into an official national baseline integrated into national environmental information systems; publish and institutionally validate the national baseline; establish its use as a mandatory reference for the design of policies, incentives, and waste- and food-waste-reduction measures; use the information generated to prioritize territorial and sectoral interventions in coherence with Targets 10 and 12.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Urban solid waste and food waste management at municipal and national levels, including national environmental information systems.",
"Target Audience": "Municipal technical teams, waste operators, key actors, representative municipalities, municipalities with greater waste generation and critical food-waste flows, and institutions responsible for national environmental information systems, policy design, incentives, and waste- and food-waste-reduction measures.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "A standardized and validated national methodology for waste and food-waste characterization; pilot studies executed in representative municipalities; trained municipal and operational actors with minimum capacities for future replication; national expansion of the methodology; an official, published, and institutionally validated national baseline on the generation and composition of urban solid waste and food waste integrated into national environmental information systems; and the use of this baseline as a mandatory reference to prioritize territorial and sectoral interventions and to design policies, incentives, and reduction measures."
panama_HR_12:
"Goal/Purpose": "By 2035, Panama will have reduced mismanaged plastic pollution by 50% through the progressive elimination of single-use plastics, strengthening the circular economy and recycling infrastructure.",
"Action/Intervention": "Operationalize the National Plastics Action Roadmap by prioritizing a focused set of high-impact and high-early-feasibility interventions for initial implementation between 2026 and 2030; establish clear institutional arrangements for implementation, specifying roles among MiAMBIENTE, municipalities, the private sector, waste managers, and base recyclers, and ensuring coherence with the current legal framework on waste and plastics; prepare enabling conditions for implementation, including operational schemes for differentiated collection, classification, and valorization of plastic waste, and mechanisms for articulation with existing or under-development economic instruments and incentives; implement the prioritized interventions in defined territories, strengthening differentiated collection, classification, and valorization of plastic waste, with emphasis on reducing mismanaged plastic pollution; apply economic and public-policy instruments that disincentivize the generation of problematic plastic waste and favor source reduction, reuse, and valorization, in coherence with the incentives defined in Target 14; monitor and report the reduction of mismanaged plastic pollution using the indicators, baselines, and methodologies established in the Plastics Roadmap, ensuring integration with national environmental information systems; progressively scale up effective interventions to new territories, adjusting operational models to local realities and strengthening local governments' capacity for sustained management; adjust regulatory, administrative, and operational frameworks related to plastics management, incorporating evidence generated during implementation and ensuring coherence with international commitments, including the Global Plastics Treaty; strengthen markets for valorized plastic materials, promoting demand stability, quality of recovered materials, and economic sustainability of recycling and reuse chains; identify territories, waste streams, or types of plastics that continue to generate high levels of pollution, and design specific corrective interventions combining operational adjustments, incentives, and environmental control; reinforce the application of existing economic and regulatory instruments to disincentivize practices that perpetuate plastic pollution, prioritizing points of the value chain where previous measures have not generated sufficient changes.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Plastics management, waste and plastics legal framework, circular economy, recycling infrastructure, differentiated collection, classification and valorization of plastic waste, national environmental information systems, and defined territories in Panama.",
"Target Audience": "MiAMBIENTE, municipalities, the private sector, waste managers, base recyclers, local governments, and actors in the recycling and reuse chains.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "A 50% reduction in mismanaged plastic pollution in Panama by 2035; progressive elimination of single-use plastics; strengthened circular economy and recycling infrastructure; strengthened differentiated collection, classification, and valorization of plastic waste; integration of monitoring and reporting into national environmental information systems; scale-up of effective interventions to new territories; strengthened markets for valorized plastic materials; and corrective interventions in territories, waste streams, or plastic types that continue to generate high levels of pollution."
panama_HR_13:
"Goal/Purpose": "Strengthen and operationalize the national biosafety framework for living modified organisms and biotechnology in Panama through clarified institutional roles, inter-institutional coordination, standardized procedures, safe management measures, integration of access and fair benefit-sharing and FPIC when genetic resources or traditional knowledge are involved, traceability, oversight, and periodic updating of biosafety measures before 2030.",
"Action/Intervention": "Carry out an exhaustive mapping of competencies, current procedures, and regulatory gaps in biosafety; identify which institution evaluates risks, authorizes, oversees, controls imports, manages incidents, and administers information related to living modified organisms and biotechnology; define and formalize through an administrative act a mechanism of inter-institutional coordination on biosafety among MiAMBIENTE, MINSA, MIDA, AUPSA, and Customs; develop a technical document for a National Biosafety Strategy that consolidates the existing framework, sets operational objectives, prioritizes biotechnology-related risks relevant to Panama, and defines a limited set of concrete measures of safe management to be implemented before 2030; adopt and operationalize standardized procedures for risk assessment and authorization of biotechnological activities, including forms, technical criteria, response times, and clearly defined institutional responsibilities; implement at least five specific measures for the safe management of biotechnology; operationally integrate the principles of access and fair benefit-sharing and FPIC into biosafety procedures when genetic resources or traditional knowledge are involved; establish a national system for the registration and traceability of authorized biotechnological activities interoperable with environmental and transparency information systems; strengthen the operational capacity of competent institutions for oversight and control in territory through inspection protocols, information exchange, and coordination among environmental, health, and customs authorities; establish a permanent technical procedure for the periodic updating of biosafety measures to incorporate new technologies, emerging risks, and lessons learned without reforming the entire regulatory framework.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Biosafety, biotechnology, living modified organisms, genetic resources, traditional knowledge, environmental, health, customs, and regulatory governance in Panama.",
"Target Audience": "MiAMBIENTE, MINSA, MIDA, AUPSA, Customs, competent institutions responsible for biosafety oversight and control, and institutions involved in the evaluation, authorization, control, follow-up, registration, traceability, and information management of biotechnological activities.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Mapped competencies, procedures, and regulatory gaps in biosafety; clear institutional roles for risk evaluation, authorization, oversight, import control, incident management, and information administration; a formalized inter-institutional coordination mechanism; a technical document for a National Biosafety Strategy; standardized and operational procedures for risk assessment and authorization; implementation of at least five specific safe management measures before 2030; integration of access and fair benefit-sharing and FPIC into relevant biosafety procedures; a national registration and traceability system interoperable with environmental and transparency information systems; strengthened institutional operational capacity for territorial oversight and control; and a permanent technical procedure for periodic updating of biosafety measures."
panama_HR_14:
"Goal/Purpose": "To exhaustively review incentives and subsidies with direct or indirect impact on biodiversity; adopt an official methodology to evaluate biodiversity impacts and classify incentives as harmful, neutral, or positive; evaluate and prioritize the most critical harmful incentives; design and implement an incentives-reform roadmap; redirect released resources toward positive incentives for biodiversity; increase the volume and scope of positive incentives; integrate biodiversity criteria into new incentives and subsidies; and publish and periodically update the inventory and status of incentives to ensure transparency and follow-up of compliance with the target.",
"Action/Intervention": "Review the analysis of fiscal, financial, budgetary, and regulatory incentives and subsidies affecting biodiversity, including in productive sectors, energy, transport, land use, and fisheries; adopt an official methodology aligned with international standards incorporating environmental, social, and economic criteria; classify incentives as harmful, neutral, or positive; evaluate and prioritize harmful incentives based on magnitude of impact, irreversibility, affected groups, and feasibility of reform; design a reform roadmap including progressive elimination, redesign, or substitution by positive incentives with fiscal, social, and territorial analysis; establish an inter-institutional mechanism for dialogue and consultation with productive sectors, local governments, indigenous peoples, civil society, and the private sector; implement the elimination or reform of at least 50% of prioritized harmful incentives through regulatory, fiscal, or administrative adjustments with transition measures for affected sectors; redirect released resources toward positive incentives for biodiversity, including payments for ecosystem services, restoration incentives, sustainable production, community conservation, and management of protected areas; increase by at least 30% the volume and scope of positive incentives, prioritizing strategic territories and vulnerable populations; integrate biodiversity criteria into new incentives and subsidies; publish and periodically update the inventory and status of incentives.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Biodiversity; productive sectors; energy; transport; land use; fisheries; strategic territories including corridors, watersheds, and coastal zones; protected areas.",
"Target Audience": "Productive sectors, local governments, indigenous peoples, civil society, the private sector, affected sectors, vulnerable populations.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Official methodology adopted for biodiversity impact evaluation and classification of incentives; prioritized list of critical harmful incentives; reform roadmap established; inter-institutional dialogue and consultation mechanism established; elimination or reform of at least 50% of prioritized harmful incentives; resources redirected toward positive biodiversity incentives; increase of at least 30% in the volume and scope of positive incentives; biodiversity criteria integrated into new incentives and subsidies; published and periodically updated inventory and status of incentives with transparency and compliance follow-up."
panama_HR_15:
"Goal/Purpose": "Delimit and prioritize critical territories of illegal deforestation to focus actions of control, restoration, and productive reconversion; agree on an inter-institutional approach for the control of illegal deforestation; integrate sustainable productive alternatives into forest landscapes; identify and prioritize incentives that favor forest conservation and sustainable landscape management; strengthen the articulation between forest monitoring and decision-making; implement integrated territorial actions in prioritized landscapes; accompany producers and local communities in adopting sustainable productive practices that reduce pressure on forests; channel financing and incentives toward territories and actors adopting sustainable management and effective forest conservation; follow up on changes in deforestation dynamics and adjust territorial strategies based on results; expand effective territorial control in critical forest landscapes; formally integrate the reduction of illegal deforestation into agricultural planning and land-use planning; strengthen long-term economic arrangements for conservation and sustainable forest management; consolidate adoption of sustainable productive alternatives in prioritized territories; focus intensive interventions on the last hotspots of illegal deforestation; reinforce deterrent and corrective measures against illegal deforestation.",
"Action/Intervention": "Use forest-monitoring information and territorial analysis to delimit and prioritize critical territories of illegal deforestation; coordinate MiAMBIENTE, MIDA, local authorities, and territorial actors for prevention, control, and follow-up; integrate silvopastoral systems, agroforestry, and sustainable forest management into forest landscapes in coordination with MIDA initiatives and rural-development programs; identify and prioritize economic and non-economic incentives aligned with Target 14; ensure forest-cover change information feeds early prevention and control actions; combine control of illegal deforestation, technical-productive accompaniment, and access to incentives in prioritized landscapes; provide continuous technical assistance to producers and local communities; channel financing and incentive mechanisms to territories and actors adopting sustainable practices; use the national monitoring system to evaluate effectiveness of measures; adjust strategies based on observed results; combine continuous forest monitoring, institutional presence, and early-response mechanisms in critical forest landscapes; integrate illegal-deforestation reduction into agricultural and land-use planning instruments so productive expansions are oriented to suitable and non-forested areas; ensure continuity, clear rules, and sufficient coverage of incentives and financial mechanisms; expand coverage of silvopastoral systems, agroforestry, and sustainable forest management; prioritize residual forest-loss hotspots for intensive interventions; ensure coherence among monitoring, oversight, and administrative sanction.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Critical territories of illegal deforestation; prioritized landscapes; forest landscapes; critical forest landscapes; intervened territories; agricultural planning and land-use planning in suitable and non-forested areas.",
"Target Audience": "MiAMBIENTE; MIDA; local authorities; territorial actors; competent entities; local governments; community actors; producers; local communities; territories and actors that adopt sustainable management and forest conservation practices.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Focused control, restoration, and productive reconversion in critical territories; coordinated prevention, control, and follow-up in prioritized areas; adoption and expansion of sustainable productive alternatives in forest landscapes; incentives and financing directed toward conservation and sustainable management; forest-monitoring information used for early prevention and control actions; reduced pressure on forests through sustainable practices; evaluation and adjustment of strategies based on deforestation dynamics; expanded territorial control and early response to illegal-deforestation alerts; productive expansion oriented exclusively to suitable and non-forested areas; continuity of economic arrangements for conservation and sustainable forest management; intensive intervention in residual hotspots of forest loss; coherent application of deterrent, corrective, oversight, and administrative sanction measures against illegal deforestation."
panama_HR_16:
"Goal/Purpose": "Build and adopt a national operational definition of organic soils for public policy and MRV purposes; develop the national baseline of organic soils and associated wetlands; design and implement an operational package of effective-conservation instruments and productive practices; establish conservation mechanisms and territorial sustainable-management programs; operationalize monitoring and verification; scale up protection/management and soil-carbon practices; integrate protection and soil-carbon criteria into territorial and productive planning; and verify progress and close gaps toward 70% of organic soils under effective protection/management and +10% soil organic carbon in prioritized agricultural lands and grasslands.",
"Action/Intervention": "Agree on technical identification criteria for peatlands, wetlands, and high-carbon soils and a minimum protocol for data collection and validation; consolidate existing information and fill priority gaps through validation in critical territories, including preliminary delimitation and prioritization by risk and carbon/biodiversity value; define intermediate targets for 2030-2033, institutional responsibilities, adoption mechanism with MIDA and IDIAP, and incentives and financing pathway aligned with Targets 14 and 28; establish effective-conservation mechanisms such as zoning, conservation agreements, wetland management, and technical restrictions on drainage and burning in critical areas; implement territorial programs for sustainable-management practices on prioritized agricultural lands and grasslands, including agroforestry and silvopastoral systems, with technical assistance from MIDA/IDIAP and selection criteria that avoid unplanned agricultural expansion; operationalize the monitoring and verification system integrating coverage indicators and measurements/estimates of soil organic carbon with interoperable reporting with national systems under Targets 21 and 25; adjust and standardize conservation instruments and productive-practice packages based on implementation lessons from 2028-2030, defining scaling criteria, operational costs, and territorial capacity requirements; scale up protection/management coverage to new prioritized territories, prioritizing hydrological connectivity and critical landscapes, and expand adoption of soil practices on agricultural lands and grasslands; integrate criteria for protection of organic soils and increase of soil carbon into sectoral and local territorial and productive planning instruments; execute a national technical verification of progress toward 70% protection/management and +10% organic carbon, identifying territorial gaps and causes; implement gap-closing measures in lagging territories, including adjustments to conservation instruments, reinforcement of productive technical assistance, and corrections of incentives driving wetland degradation or soil-carbon loss.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Organic soils, associated wetlands, peatlands, high-carbon soils, prioritized agricultural lands, grasslands, critical territories, critical landscapes, and territories with hydrological connectivity.",
"Target Audience": "MiAMBIENTE, MIDA, IDIAP, local governments, territorial actors, prioritized agricultural lands and grasslands managers, and institutions responsible for public policy, MRV, adaptation/monitoring systems, and territorial and productive planning.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "A national operational definition and baseline for organic soils and associated wetlands; agreed technical criteria and data protocols; effective-conservation instruments and productive-practice packages adopted and standardized; territorial programs implemented; interoperable monitoring and verification system operational; protection/management coverage expanded to prioritized territories; protection and soil-carbon criteria integrated into planning instruments; national technical verification completed; territorial gaps identified and addressed; progress toward 70% of organic soils under effective protection/management and +10% soil organic carbon in prioritized agricultural lands and grasslands."
panama_HR_17:
"Goal/Purpose": "Transform agri-food systems in 21 priority districts through climate-smart and sustainable productive practices, ensuring coherence with adaptation, mitigation, and conservation targets.",
"Action/Intervention": "Define technical and climate criteria for selecting the 21 priority districts; identify viable climate-smart productive practices within prioritized districts, aligned with the PNCCSA and MIDA policies; implement pilot agri-food transformation programs integrating sustainable productive practices, technical accompaniment, field validation, and participation of local producers; strengthen agricultural extension and technical assistance services using the capacities of MIDA, IDIAP, and technical partners; monitor adoption of practices, changes in productivity, resilience, and reduction of environmental pressures using existing agroclimatic and territorial information systems; evaluate pilot program results to identify the most effective practices, territories, and models; progressively scale up validated sustainable agri-food practices to new producers within prioritized districts, linking them with value chains and markets; integrate agri-food transformation into MIDA's sectoral policies and territorial plans.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Agri-food systems in 21 priority districts within the agricultural sector.",
"Target Audience": "MIDA, IDIAP, technical partners, local producers, and new producers within the prioritized districts.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Selection of 21 priority districts based on climate vulnerability, pressure on ecosystems, productive importance, and local capacities; identification and adoption of viable climate-smart productive practices; implementation and evaluation of pilot programs; strengthened agricultural extension and technical assistance services; monitored changes in productivity, resilience, and reduction of environmental pressures; scaling up of validated practices linked with value chains and markets; integration of agri-food transformation into sectoral policies and territorial plans."
panama_HR_18:
"Goal/Purpose": "Increase urban green and blue spaces through a national baseline, prioritization criteria, technical guidelines, integration into Local Land-Use Plans, pilot interventions, monitoring, municipal management mechanisms, scaling up, and incorporation into national adaptation and urban-planning updates, ensuring continuity beyond 2030 and defining guidelines for expansion after 2035.",
"Action/Intervention": "Build a national baseline of urban green and blue spaces; establish methodology and key indicators of coverage, access, and quality; articulate municipal, metropolitan, and sectoral information to generate an official reference valid for 2027; define technical and social criteria to identify priority municipalities and neighborhoods based on climate vulnerability, deficit of green areas, and population density; establish national technical guidelines for incorporating green and blue infrastructure into Local Land-Use Plans aligned with the National Adaptation Plan for the Human Settlements Sector; explicitly integrate green and blue infrastructure criteria into the Local Land-Use Plans of prioritized municipalities and ensure formal adoption by local authorities; implement pilot interventions for creation and recovery of urban green and blue spaces, including parks, green corridors, urban wetlands, and sustainable drainage, with emphasis on risk reduction and equitable access; monitor the increase in surface of urban green and blue spaces and their contribution to reducing climate vulnerability using territorial and climate-information systems; formalize municipal mechanisms for management and maintenance, including institutional responsibilities, operational budgets, and community-participation schemes; scale up green and blue infrastructure solutions to new neighborhoods and municipalities while strengthening technical and management capacities in local governments; integrate evaluation results into updates of the National Adaptation Plan for the Human Settlements Sector and the next cycle of urban-planning instruments; define technical guidelines for subsequent expansion after 2035.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Urban green and blue spaces; green and blue infrastructure; human settlements sector; Local Land-Use Plans; urban planning.",
"Target Audience": "National authorities, local authorities, municipalities, metropolitan and sectoral entities, local governments, prioritized municipalities and neighborhoods, and communities participating in management and maintenance schemes.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "An official national reference on urban green and blue spaces valid for 2027; identified priority municipalities and neighborhoods; national technical guidelines established; green and blue infrastructure criteria formally adopted in Local Land-Use Plans of prioritized municipalities; pilot interventions implemented; effective increase in the surface of urban green and blue spaces monitored; contribution to reduction of climate vulnerability monitored; municipal management and maintenance mechanisms formalized with assigned responsibilities, budgets, and community participation; green and blue infrastructure solutions scaled to new neighborhoods and municipalities; evaluation results integrated into updates of the National Adaptation Plan for the Human Settlements Sector and future urban-planning instruments; technical guidelines defined for expansion after 2035."
panama_HR_19:
"Goal/Purpose": "Establish and implement operational Multi-hazard Early Warning Systems and anticipatory action mechanisms in 10 prioritized vulnerable regions, with defined standards, roles, information flows, protocols, financing, accessibility, and performance monitoring.",
"Action/Intervention": "Define the national framework of Multi-hazard Early Warning Systems; identify and prioritize 10 vulnerable regions; develop the draft EWS and Anticipatory Actions roadmap; integrate climate, hydrological, coastal, and territorial information; design anticipatory-action protocols linking warning levels with decisions, responsibilities, and preventive measures; design financing mechanisms for anticipatory action; implement operational Multi-hazard Early Warning Systems in the 10 prioritized regions; activate mechanisms for anticipatory action and local financing; ensure accessibility of information through appropriate channels, languages, and formats; monitor and evaluate system performance and incorporate feedback.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Multi-hazard early warning systems, anticipatory action, climate, hydrological, coastal, and territorial information systems.",
"Target Audience": "Authorities, communities, producers, and local authorities in the 10 prioritized vulnerable regions.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Operational Multi-hazard Early Warning Systems established in 10 prioritized regions; anticipatory action and local financing mechanisms activated for early responses based on forecasts and risk scenarios; accessible information for communities, producers, and local authorities; improved system accuracy, response times, and effectiveness through monitoring and feedback."
panama_HR_20:
"Goal/Purpose": "Finalize the Adaptation Plan for the Energy Sector and integrate climate resilience into energy-sector planning, operation, maintenance, emergency response, and regulatory processes so that current and future climate vulnerabilities are considered in decision-making.",
"Action/Intervention": "Review current energy-planning instruments to identify where and how climate scenarios, physical risks, and resilience criteria should be incorporated into expansion, operation, and maintenance decisions; define technical criteria of climate resilience for generation, transmission, and distribution infrastructure, including risk thresholds, design standards, and adaptation priorities for extreme climate events; incorporate climate scenarios and physical-risk analysis into formal national energy-planning processes; prioritize and implement adaptation measures in critical energy infrastructure exposed to elevated climate risks such as floods, droughts, and landslides; integrate the energy sector into national protocols for early warning and response to climate emergencies, with clear operational roles for generators, transmitters, and distributors; evaluate energy-system performance during climate events using resilience indicators such as duration of interruptions, areas affected, and recovery times to adjust technical and operational criteria; integrate climate-resilience criteria permanently into the technical and regulatory framework of the energy sector so their application is mandatory in planning, operation, and maintenance; institutionalize a periodic mechanism for review and updating of climate resilience aligned with new climate scenarios and operational lessons.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Energy sector, including energy infrastructure for generation, transmission, and distribution, and national energy planning and regulatory frameworks.",
"Target Audience": "Generators, transmitters, distributors, national energy-planning authorities, and entities responsible for the technical and regulatory framework of the energy sector.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Climate scenarios, physical risks, and resilience criteria are incorporated into energy-system expansion, operation, and maintenance decisions; technical climate-resilience criteria are established for energy infrastructure; adaptation measures are implemented in critical infrastructure exposed to climate risks; the energy sector is integrated into early warning and climate-emergency response protocols; energy-system performance is evaluated using resilience indicators; climate-resilience criteria become mandatory in the sector’s technical and regulatory framework; and a periodic review and updating mechanism for energy-system climate resilience is institutionalized."
panama_HR_21:
"Goal/Purpose": "Formalize OSIGA (Integrated Agroclimatic Management System Observatory) as the central national platform for agroclimatic information and ensure its use in planning, coordination, and risk management.",
"Action/Intervention": "Formalize the operational mandate of OSIGA, defining responsibilities, information flows, and inter-institutional coordination mechanisms; technically integrate the Climate Risk Atlas and other relevant systems into OSIGA, ensuring database interoperability, common standards, and periodic information updating; strengthen and standardize the operation of the Agroclimatic Technical Roundtables, defining clear protocols for the use of agroclimatic information in territorial decisions, productive planning, and risk management; integrate OSIGA as a mandatory input in the formulation and implementation of local and regional adaptation plans and agri-food-system transformation programs; strengthen OSIGA's interoperability with early-warning systems, adaptation-monitoring systems, and territorial observatories, ensuring bidirectional information flows; train territorial technicians and decision-makers in the systematic use of agroclimatic information for planning, investment, and response to extreme events.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Agroclimatic information management, territorial planning, adaptation planning, risk management, and agri-food-system transformation.",
"Target Audience": "OSIGA, inter-institutional actors involved in coordination mechanisms, Agroclimatic Technical Roundtables, territorial technicians, decision-makers, and actors involved in local and regional adaptation plans, early-warning systems, adaptation-monitoring systems, territorial observatories, and agri-food-system transformation programs.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "OSIGA operates as the central national platform for agroclimatic information with defined responsibilities, interoperable databases, common standards, periodic information updates, standardized roundtable operations, mandatory use in adaptation plans and agri-food-system transformation programs, bidirectional information flows with related systems, and strengthened capacity of territorial technicians and decision-makers to use agroclimatic information."
panama_HR_22:
"Goal/Purpose": "Define and validate a standardized methodology for Local and Regional Adaptation Plans; identify and prioritize territories for plan development or updating; develop and formally integrate Local and Regional Adaptation Plans into development and watershed management plans; implement priority adaptation actions; and channel financing for plan implementation.",
"Action/Intervention": "Define a standardized methodology for Local and Regional Adaptation Plans, including minimum contents, territorial prioritization criteria, participatory approach, gender integration, social safeguards, and alignment with development plans and watershed management; identify and prioritize territories based on climate vulnerability, ecological value, provision of ecosystem services, water-resource protection, presence of protected areas, coastal zones, and indigenous territories; articulate climate, risk, and territorial information from OSIGA, early-warning systems, and environmental monitoring for local planning; develop pilot adaptation plans in an initial group of prioritized territories to validate the methodology and adjust approaches; establish territorial governance arrangements for each pilot plan, defining roles of local governments, communities, traditional authorities, sectoral entities, and MiAMBIENTE; develop at least 8 Local and Regional Adaptation Plans in prioritized territories; formally integrate adaptation plans into local and regional development plans and watershed management plans; develop at least 4 Local and Regional Adaptation Plans in prioritized territories; implement priority adaptation actions identified in the plans, including nature-based solutions, risk management, productive adaptation, and strengthening of ecosystem services; channel specific financing for implementation using the mechanisms defined in Target 28 and aligning public, private, and cooperation resources.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Prioritized territories, including areas identified by climate vulnerability, ecological value, ecosystem services provision, water-resource protection, protected areas, coastal zones, indigenous territories, and watershed management domains.",
"Target Audience": "Local governments, communities, traditional authorities, sectoral entities, MiAMBIENTE, and prioritized territories where Local and Regional Adaptation Plans will be developed or updated.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "A standardized and validated methodology for Local and Regional Adaptation Plans; prioritized territories identified for plan development or updating; climate, risk, and territorial information consistently used for local planning; pilot plans developed and governance arrangements established; at least 8 Local and Regional Adaptation Plans developed in prioritized territories; at least 4 Local and Regional Adaptation Plans developed in prioritized territories; adaptation plans formally integrated into local and regional development plans and watershed management plans with binding character; priority adaptation actions implemented; and specific financing channeled for plan implementation."
panama_HR_23:
"Goal/Purpose": "Publish and implement the Marine-Coastal Adaptation Plan; articulate marine-coastal adaptation with local planning; ensure coherence with the Local and Regional Adaptation Plans (Target 22) and coastal-development plans; integrate coastal-adaptation measures into the management of the marine SINAP; and channel specific financing for marine-coastal adaptation.",
"Action/Intervention": "Publication of the Marine-Coastal Adaptation Plan; articulate marine-coastal adaptation with local planning; establish local governance arrangements for implementation, defining the roles of local governments, coastal communities, traditional authorities, MiAMBIENTE, and other sectoral entities; implement marine-coastal adaptation interventions with Nature-based Solutions in prioritized zones, prioritizing the restoration of mangroves, dunes, and coastal wetlands, and strengthening natural protection in the face of extreme events and sea-level rise; integrate coastal-adaptation measures into the management of the marine SINAP; channel specific financing for marine-coastal adaptation using the mechanisms defined in Target 28 and aligning public, private, and cooperation resources.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Marine-coastal areas, prioritized coastal zones, mangroves, dunes, coastal wetlands, and the marine SINAP.",
"Target Audience": "Local governments, coastal communities, traditional authorities, MiAMBIENTE, other sectoral entities, and public, private, and cooperation financing actors.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Coherence between marine-coastal adaptation, Local and Regional Adaptation Plans, and coastal-development plans; local governance arrangements for implementation with defined roles; implementation of Nature-based Solutions in prioritized zones; restoration of mangroves, dunes, and coastal wetlands; strengthened natural protection against extreme events and sea-level rise; integration of coastal-adaptation measures into marine SINAP management; and channeling of specific financing for marine-coastal adaptation."
panama_HR_24:
"Goal/Purpose": "Integrate climate information into national epidemiological surveillance and health-sector adaptation planning to support the prevention, early detection, and response to climate-sensitive health risks, and ensure continuity and improvement of the climate-health approach beyond 2030.",
"Action/Intervention": "Finalize the National Adaptation Plan for the Health Sector; define priority climate variables (temperature, precipitation, extreme events) for incorporation into national epidemiological surveillance; design a national methodology for integrating climate information into epidemiological surveillance systems, including roles, information flows, and use criteria for health decisions; incorporate climate variables and projections into the epidemiological surveillance systems of prioritized health facilities, ensuring interoperability with climate- and risk-information systems; train health personnel in the use of climate information for prevention, early detection, and response to climate-sensitive health risks, prioritizing regions of high vulnerability; formalize sectoral protocols for using integrated climate and epidemiological information to activate preventive measures, contingency plans, and inter-institutional coordination; expand climate-health integration to the rest of the public health network, ensuring methodological consistency and data quality in at least 80% of health facilities; integrate climate-sensitive health indicators into national systems for adaptation and loss-and-damage monitoring, guaranteeing periodic reporting; incorporate evaluation results into updates of sectoral health and adaptation plans.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Health sector; national epidemiological surveillance systems; public health network; adaptation and loss-and-damage monitoring systems.",
"Target Audience": "Health personnel; prioritized health facilities; the rest of the public health network; institutions involved in epidemiological surveillance, climate information, risk information, and inter-institutional coordination.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Priority climate variables are precisely defined and incorporated into epidemiological surveillance; a national methodology for climate-information integration is established; prioritized health facilities incorporate climate variables and projections with interoperability across climate- and risk-information systems; health personnel are trained, especially in regions of high vulnerability; sectoral protocols are formalized for preventive measures, contingency plans, and coordination; climate-health integration is expanded across the public health network with methodological consistency and data quality in at least 80% of health facilities; climate-sensitive health indicators are periodically reported in national adaptation and loss-and-damage monitoring systems; evaluation results are incorporated into updated sectoral health and adaptation plans, supporting continuity and improvement beyond 2030."
panama_HR_25:
"Goal/Purpose": "Strengthen and operationalize climate adaptation and Loss and Damage monitoring, evaluation, data governance, interoperability, reporting, and regulatory/procedural frameworks for decision-making and transparency.",
"Action/Intervention": "Formalize institutional agreements on indicator data flows, prioritizing indicators with yellow/red traffic-light status and those most used in public decision-making; develop the draft regulatory framework for the Planned Relocation protocol; install a universal data-collection scheme with field templates and an interoperable repository to reduce duplication and standardize climate-change and Loss and Damage variables; finalize the Loss and Damage section in the National Climate Transparency Platform (PNTC); design the climate-displacement component, including cooperation and data-flow agreements, event typology, minimum variables, and reporting pathway; evaluate the functionality of the Adaptation M&E system and the Loss and Damage subsystem with external technical cooperation, including gap analysis, interoperability, roles, sustainability, and costs; improve data sources and quality through cleansing of series, validation rules, quality control, and an annual recalculation cycle with data providers; issue or adopt the Ministerial Resolution on technical aspects, or ensure its effective implementation through manuals, leads, schedule, and institutional compliance; operate the M&E Module in the PNTC with recalculation executed by data providers, including annual calendar, cross-validation, and publication; achieve interoperability with the Risk Observatory through a shared data dictionary, API/ETL, and a joint risk-measures-results-Loss and Damage dashboard; implement pilot projects to evaluate the effectiveness of measures versus the quantification of Loss and Damage by sector/territory, including equipment and evaluation methodology; operationalize the Planned Relocation Protocol through last-alternative criteria, pathway of rights/livelihoods/services, institutional roles, and financing mechanisms; publish the annual M&E dashboard covering adaptation and Loss and Damage with updated information for decision-making and transparency.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Climate adaptation, Loss and Damage, climate displacement, planned relocation, monitoring and evaluation systems, data management and interoperability, national climate transparency and risk information systems.",
"Target Audience": "Institutions responsible for indicator data provision and validation, data providers, institutions subject to ministerial resolution compliance, the National Climate Transparency Platform (PNTC), the Risk Observatory, external technical cooperation actors, and public decision-makers.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Institutionalized data-flow agreements; a draft and operational procedure for the Planned Relocation Protocol; a universal and interoperable data-collection and repository scheme; a finalized Loss and Damage section in the PNTC; a designed climate-displacement component; an evaluated Adaptation M&E system and Loss and Damage subsystem with identified gaps, roles, sustainability, and costs; improved data quality through cleansing, validation, quality control, and annual recalculation; implementation or effective application of the Ministerial Resolution; operation of the PNTC M&E Module with recalculation, cross-validation, and publication; interoperability with the Risk Observatory and a joint dashboard; pilot evaluations of measures versus Loss and Damage quantification; and annual publication of an updated adaptation and Loss and Damage dashboard for decision-making and transparency."
panama_HR_26:
"Goal/Purpose": "Formally constitute and operationalize the National Integrated Marine-Coastal and Wetlands Monitoring System; integrate existing monitoring efforts and databases; establish standardized national protocols, inventories, cartography, indices, monitoring systems, platform, and financing to support marine-coastal planning, conservation, management of the marine SINAP, and climate-change adaptation.",
"Action/Intervention": "Constitute the system through an administrative instrument defining objectives, mandatory components, institutional roles, data flow and custody, minimum standards, reporting frequency, and annual operational scheme; carry out and consolidate a national inventory of existing marine-coastal and wetlands monitoring initiatives and databases; adopt standardized national protocols and an integrated sampling design for seagrass and coral reefs, wetlands, sea turtles, and marine water quality; design the National Marine Water Quality Index; generate preliminary national cartography of seagrass and coral reefs with field validation and define permanent monitoring zones under MiAMBIENTE's coordination; define the methodology and structure of the National Wetlands Inventory and establish a survey and validation plan; design the National Sea Turtle Monitoring System; put into operation the system's National Platform with repository, dashboards, and periodic reports; complete and publish the official National Map of Seagrass and Coral Reefs and establish a national network of sentinel sites; update and publish the official National Wetlands Inventory and implement a periodic monitoring plan; implement the National Sea Turtle Monitoring System with a standardized national database and management measures linked to fisheries regulation and control; implement the National Marine Water Quality Index through monitoring campaigns in priority coastal zones and marine SINAP areas; ensure permanent financing for technical personnel, field campaigns, laboratory analysis, platform, and reporting through public budget and national environmental financial mechanisms.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Marine-coastal and wetlands environments, including seagrass and coral reefs, coastal and continental wetlands, sea turtle nesting and feeding sites, marine water quality in priority coastal zones and areas of the marine SINAP, and related national environmental and geospatial information platforms.",
"Target Audience": "MiAMBIENTE; governmental, academic, and NGO entities involved in marine-coastal and wetlands monitoring; decision-makers; marine-coastal planning authorities; managers of the marine SINAP; fisheries regulation and control authorities.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "A formally established and operational national monitoring system; integrated monitoring efforts and reduced duplication; standardized protocols and interoperable data; a National Marine Water Quality Index in use; preliminary and official national cartography of seagrass and coral reefs; an official National Wetlands Inventory with periodic monitoring; an operational National Sea Turtle Monitoring System with a standardized national database and management measures in critical zones; a functioning national platform with repository, dashboards, and periodic reports; a national network of sentinel sites; monitoring results integrated into marine-coastal planning, conservation, fisheries management, marine SINAP management, and climate adaptation; and permanent financing for system operation."

{
  "Goal/Purpose": "Regulate and operationalize the Climate Risk Observatory at the national level and establish, pilot, adjust, scale up, and consolidate a territorial network of observatories/units and early meteorological warning systems integrated into territorial planning, financing, and the national M&E system.",
  "Action/Intervention": "Define the Observatory architecture, including components, tools, dashboards, data standards, institutional roles, access rules, updating protocols, and the official set of adaptation, loss, and damage indicators aligned with Target 25; design the operational model with minimum services, protocols for accompanying local governments, criteria for territorial prioritization, and a standard package of tools; constitute the Community Resilience Technical Team and define its coordination with universities, CSOs, municipalities, and community councils; formalize territorial alliances through framework agreements for hosting and operating observatories; design the Network of Early Meteorological Warning Systems in coordination with IMHPA and SINAPROC, including priority municipalities/watersheds, activation and response protocols, communication channels, and interoperability and coverage requirements; agree with ASEP and mobile-telephony operators on interoperability and mass-diffusion of warnings; implement pilot observatories in prioritized regions with technical focal points, annual work plans, local attention mechanisms, and capacity to accompany adaptation projects including NbS; operate early-warning systems in pilot territories with simulation exercises, community-communication protocols, and feedback mechanisms; integrate climate analysis into territorial planning and local investment prioritization with support from territorial observatories and national guidelines linked to Target 22; systematize and report territorial information on resilience, vulnerability, and implemented measures using standardized formats and delivery pathways to feed the Climate Risk Observatory and Target 25 M&E system; adjust the model based on pilot evaluation and document costs, capacities, barriers, and lessons learned; scale up the observatory network to new regions using consistent methodologies; consolidate a continuous territorial capacity-strengthening program with standardized curricula and alliances with universities/NGOs; strengthen technical and operational interoperability between territorial observatories and the Climate Risk Observatory through improved automation, dashboards, and comparative territorial analysis; integrate the territorial network into planning and financing mechanisms so projects and investments use observatory technical assistance and report through the national M&E system; ensure the verifiable operation of at least 10 observatories/units with minimum standards.",
  "Ecosystem/Area": "Climate risk management, territorial planning, adaptation, loss and damage monitoring, early meteorological warning systems, resilience and vulnerability reporting, municipal/watershed-level and national climate-information systems.",
  "Target Audience": "National-level institutions responsible for the Climate Risk Observatory; territorial observatories/units; local governments; municipalities; community councils; universities; CSOs; NGOs; IMHPA; SINAPROC; ASEP; mobile-telephony operators; prioritized territories/regions, municipalities, and watersheds; communities.",
  "Expected Impact/Outcome": "A nationally regulated and operational Climate Risk Observatory with standardized architecture, indicators, and data flows; pilot and scaled territorial observatories/units and early-warning systems functioning with defined minimum standards; formalized territorial alliances and a constituted Community Resilience Technical Team; climate risk integrated into district planning and local investment prioritization; standardized territorial reporting feeding the national M&E system and Climate Risk Observatory with periodic quality verification; improved interoperability, automation, comparative territorial analysis, and warning diffusion; a continuous territorial capacity-strengthening program in place; and verifiable operation of at least 10 observatories/units with active technical assistance, support for adaptation projects, operational municipal/watershed EWS, integration into territorial planning, and periodic reporting to the national Observatory."
}

"Goal/Purpose": "Formalize and operationalize the financial architecture of the Nature Pledge by defining the roles, governance, eligibility criteria, and alignment of the Fondo Panamá Natural, the Fondo Reforesta, and other financial vehicles with climate, biodiversity, and land targets; strengthen institutional and financial management capacities; establish coordinated, stable, multi-source capitalization; and ensure transparent, safeguarded, and long-term financing for prioritized conservation, restoration, adaptation, mitigation, and community development actions.",
"Action/Intervention": "Define the specific role of the Fondo Panamá Natural, the Fondo Reforesta, and other financial vehicles, including their governance mechanisms, eligibility criteria, and alignment with climate, biodiversity, and land targets; strengthen institutional capacities for trust fund management, capital mobilization, and financial administration; review and update the operating regulations of the Fondo Reforesta to simplify processes, clarify roles, update eligibility requirements, reduce procedures, and establish maximum evaluation and disbursement timeframes; approve the final version of the Conservation and Community Development Plan of the Fondo Panamá Natural; develop a national portfolio of reforestation, restoration, and agroforestry projects aligned with priority regions, degraded areas, implementing actors, and the Conservation and Community Development Plan; design and approve the governance model of the Fondo Panamá Natural, including institutional roles, participation mechanisms, administrative processes, and coordination guidelines with the Fondo Reforesta; prepare and formalize the legal agreement of the Fondo Panamá Natural establishing obligations, closing conditions, long-term financial commitments, and stability provisions; establish a permanent technical team to support project formulation, follow-up, and evaluation under the Fondo Reforesta and strengthen capacities of implementing actors in territory; align existing fiscal and financial incentives with the Nature Pledge architecture in coordination with the incentives reform of Target 14; establish social, environmental, and gender safeguards; capitalize and put into full operation the Fondo Panamá Natural and the Fondo Reforesta with stable financial flows from public, private, and international cooperation sources; mobilize at least USD 300 million toward prioritized actions; implement innovative financing mechanisms including PES, biodiversity credits, and carbon markets with monitoring, reporting, and verification systems; and publish periodic financing and impact reports to guarantee transparency, accountability, and trust.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Nature finance, conservation, community development, reforestation, restoration, agroforestry, protected areas, degraded areas, climate, biodiversity, land, territorial adaptation, and mitigation.",
"Target Audience": "Fondo Panamá Natural, Fondo Reforesta, other financial vehicles under the Nature Pledge, institutions responsible for trust fund management and financial administration, implementing actors in territory, the National System of Protected Areas, local communities, indigenous peoples, vulnerable groups, investors, civil society, and public, private, and international cooperation financing sources.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "A formalized and coordinated financial architecture for the Nature Pledge; updated and simplified operating regulations for the Fondo Reforesta; an approved Conservation and Community Development Plan for the Fondo Panamá Natural; a national portfolio of reforestation, restoration, and agroforestry projects aligned with priority regions and degraded areas; an approved governance model and formal legal agreement for the Fondo Panamá Natural; a permanent technical support team for Fondo Reforesta projects; aligned fiscal and financial incentives; established social, environmental, and gender safeguards; full capitalization and operation of the Fondo Panamá Natural and the Fondo Reforesta; mobilization of at least USD 300 million for prioritized actions; implementation of PES, biodiversity credits, and carbon markets with monitoring, reporting, and verification systems; and periodic public reporting on financing and impacts to ensure transparency, accountability, and trust."
panama_HR_29:
"Goal/Purpose": "To harmonize implementation of the Escazú Agreement with the Nature Pledge governance framework; design and implement a national mechanism for the protection of environmental defenders; integrate access-to-information principles into national information and monitoring systems; guarantee effective public participation and access to environmental justice in Nature Pledge implementation; define aligned indicators on access to information, participation, protection of defenders, and gender equity; incorporate equitable representation and a gender approach into Nature Pledge decision-making spaces; and consolidate local capacities for mediation, community accompaniment, and preventive conflict management.",
"Action/Intervention": "Harmonize the national Roadmap for implementation of the Escazú Agreement with the governance framework defined in Target 30, including identification of institutional responsibilities, articulation points, and operational gaps; design the national mechanism for protection of environmental defenders, including institutional architecture, complaint pathways, activation criteria, protection measures, and inter-institutional coordination, based on Article 9 of the Escazú Agreement and current national regulations; integrate Escazú Agreement principles on access to environmental information into national information and monitoring systems, ensuring coherence with Target 25 and ANTAI roles; develop operational protocols for effective public participation and access to environmental justice in implementation of Nature Pledge targets, prioritizing territories with high socio-environmental conflict; define indicators of access to information, effective participation, protection of defenders, and gender equity aligned with the national system for monitoring adaptation, loss, and damage; implement the national mechanism for protection of environmental defenders in prioritized territories and articulate it with the community resilience observatories defined in Target 27; implement territorial mechanisms for access to information, participation, and environmental justice through public environmental-information platforms, territorial outreach and participation events, and technical and legal accompaniment schemes for communities and vulnerable groups in prioritized territories; incorporate mandatory criteria of equitable representation and a gender approach into regulations, terms of reference, and designation mechanisms of Nature Pledge decision-making spaces and apply them at national and territorial levels; consolidate local capacities for mediation, community accompaniment, and preventive management of conflicts linked to environmental projects.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Environmental governance, access to environmental information, public participation, environmental justice, protection of environmental defenders, national information and monitoring systems, Nature Pledge decision-making spaces, and prioritized territories with high socio-environmental conflict.",
"Target Audience": "Institutions responsible for the Escazú Agreement Roadmap and Nature Pledge governance framework; ANTAI; entities involved in the national mechanism for protection of environmental defenders; Nature Pledge decision-making spaces at national and territorial levels; communities and vulnerable groups in prioritized territories; environmental defenders; and local actors involved in mediation, accompaniment, and conflict prevention.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Institutional responsibilities, articulation points, and operational gaps identified; a designed and operational national mechanism for protection of environmental defenders; Escazú access-to-information principles integrated into national information and monitoring systems; operational protocols established for public participation and access to environmental justice; indicators defined and aligned with the national monitoring system for adaptation, loss, and damage; territorial mechanisms for access to information, participation, and justice implemented in prioritized territories; equitable representation and gender approach incorporated and applied in Nature Pledge decision-making spaces; and strengthened local capacities for mediation, community accompaniment, and preventive conflict management."

"Goal/Purpose": "Finalize, adopt, operationalize, endorse, submit, approve, promulgate, regulate, and establish the legal, regulatory, monitoring, and institutional framework for climate change, green transition, nature pledge implementation, and unified governance at the national level.",
"Action/Intervention": "Finalize the technical, inter-institutional, and participatory consultation process of the draft Climate Change and Green Transition Framework Law; formally adopt the Nature Pledge through an administrative instrument establishing its national-level implementation; develop, integrate, and operationalize a Nature Pledge monitoring module in the National Climate Transparency Platform to ensure traceability of targets, indicators, and progress by implementation phase, articulated with structural targets and the regulatory implementation package of the Pact; obtain political endorsement from the Executive Branch (Ministry of the Presidency, Cabinet Council) for the regulatory package; formally submit to the National Assembly the draft Framework Law, the Environmental Non-regression Law, and provisions on the Pact and unified governance; drive legislative approval and promulgation of the Framework Law; develop and approve priority regulations of the Framework Law focused on planning instruments, information and monitoring systems, and inter-institutional coordination mechanisms; establish the National Climate, Biodiversity, and Land Committee as a technical and participatory body with multi-sectoral representation and clear advisory, follow-up, and technical coherence functions.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Climate change, green transition, nature, biodiversity, land, environmental governance, legislative and regulatory framework, monitoring and transparency systems, and inter-institutional coordination at the national level.",
"Target Audience": "Executive Branch (Ministry of the Presidency, Cabinet Council), National Assembly, national-level institutions involved in consultation and inter-institutional coordination, the National Climate Transparency Platform, and the National Climate, Biodiversity, and Land Committee.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "A finalized consultation process for the draft Framework Law; formal national adoption of the Nature Pledge; an operational monitoring module in the National Climate Transparency Platform with traceability of targets, indicators, and progress by implementation phase; political endorsement of the regulatory package by the Executive Branch; formal submission of the draft Framework Law, Environmental Non-regression Law, and provisions on the Pact and unified governance to the National Assembly; legislative approval and promulgation of the Framework Law; approved priority regulations focused on planning instruments, information and monitoring systems, and inter-institutional coordination mechanisms; and establishment of the National Climate, Biodiversity, and Land Committee with multi-sectoral representation and defined advisory, follow-up, and technical coherence functions."

"Goal/Purpose": "Develop a law and comprehensive strategy for the green transition and for facing climate change by 2050 so that Panama's economy and society take the necessary measures to prosper despite the climate crisis, biodiversity loss, desertification, and pollution.",
"Action/Intervention": "Create a national cabinet with representatives from State entities to local authorities for management and planning of actions and for promoting a joint implementation and investment framework at national and regional level; carry out vulnerability assessments of critical infrastructure such as ports, transport and energy systems to adapt it to climate change impacts; systematize, improve, and modernize measurement, reporting, and verification processes for data and information related to the green transition and climate action, ensuring access and availability for all Panamanians and prioritizing scientific data for adaptation measures; establish a national climate and environmental early-warning system focused on communities in flood-, drought-, extreme temperature-, and coastal-risk areas, reaching 80% of at-risk communities, accompanied by continuous disaster risk reduction training; establish community resilience centers in each region with authorities and local partners for disaster preparedness and recovery support; restore degraded ecosystems and key watersheds in the Azuero Peninsula; adopt international standards for transparent reporting of climate-risk management in the financial and business sectors; regulate and capitalize the National Adaptation Fund to finance community resilience and preparedness initiatives; back and finance research initiatives in restoration, conservation, climate change, sustainable agriculture, clean energy, reduction of plastic use, and biodiversity protection.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "National climate governance and planning; critical infrastructure including ports, transport and energy systems; data and information systems; at-risk communities in flood-, drought-, extreme temperature-, and coastal-prone areas; regional community resilience systems; degraded ecosystems and key watersheds in the Azuero Peninsula; financial and business sectors; research and innovation in restoration, conservation, sustainable agriculture, clean energy, plastic reduction, and biodiversity protection.",
"Target Audience": "State entities, local authorities, national and regional authorities, all Panamanians, communities located in at-risk areas, authorities and local partners in each region, the financial and business sectors, and community initiatives receiving support from the National Adaptation Fund.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "A law and comprehensive strategy for the green transition and climate action by 2050; a national cabinet empowered for coordinated management and planning; vulnerability assessments completed for critical infrastructure to support adaptation; improved and modernized measurement, reporting, and verification processes with public access to information; a national climate and environmental early-warning system reaching 80% of at-risk communities with continuous disaster risk reduction training; community resilience centers established in each region; restored degraded ecosystems and key watersheds in the Azuero Peninsula to guarantee human consumption, agriculture, health, and regional development; adoption of international standards for transparent climate-risk reporting in financial and business sectors; a regulated and capitalized National Adaptation Fund financing community resilience initiatives; and financed research initiatives supporting innovation in the specified areas."

"Action/Intervention": "Present to the UN a unified international commitment for the protection of nature (\"Nature Pledge\") with climate, biodiversity, and desertification targets; promote inter-territorial and intercultural alliances among local communities, civil society, indigenous peoples, faith groups, and other key actors; lead participatory national processes involving all sectors of society; promote collaborations on environmental and climate issues with MERCOSUR, Small Island Developing States (SIDS), and other like-minded nations; form a high-level commission to drive national and global measures for decarbonizing international maritime and air transport; ratify the High Seas Treaty (BBNJ); reaffirm and adopt the Global Plastics Treaty; ensure effective and coordinated management of the Eastern Tropical Pacific Marine Corridor (CMAR) with neighboring countries.",

"Target Audience": "Panama; the UN; local communities; civil society; indigenous peoples; faith groups; other key actors; all sectors of society; MERCOSUR countries; Small Island Developing States (SIDS); other like-minded nations; neighboring countries.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Panama becomes the first country in the world to present a unified international commitment for nature protection with climate, biodiversity, and desertification targets; knowledge and sustainable practices are exchanged and joint actions are executed; all sectors of society contribute to discussion on the country's green and blue future; countries face common challenges, share experiences, and develop joint strategies; national and global measures for decarbonizing international maritime and air transport are driven; commitment to conservation of marine biodiversity in international waters is cemented; production and consumption of single-use plastics are significantly reduced and sustainable alternatives are promoted; key ecosystems are protected through effective and coordinated CMAR management for marine conservation and resource sustainability."

"Action/Intervention": "Promote the establishment of a monitoring system for the CHCP's ecosystems; continue environmental education and training programs for the CHCP's communities; promote the preparation/updating and implementation of management plans for the CHCP's sub-watersheds; develop a collaboration agreement to drive the management and conservation of protected areas; prepare a comprehensive plan for the prevention of logging and burning, with a multi-year investment program and a monitoring scheme.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "CHCP's ecosystems, CHCP's communities, CHCP's sub-watersheds, and protected areas.",
"Target Audience": "CHCP's communities.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Establishment of an ecosystem monitoring system; continuity of environmental education and training programs; preparation/updating and implementation of sub-watershed management plans; a collaboration agreement for the management and conservation of protected areas; and a comprehensive prevention plan for logging and burning with a multi-year investment program and monitoring scheme."
